verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD 1f32e2c (the only changes since 7061d55 are STATUS.md and history/). I used a git-archive copy at scratchpad/review2v/tree, and the scripts are s/m1.js, m1b.js and m1c.js. At every face factor, compute_limits.scoreAt draws the arms at max(35, rest+2) = 92°. measureViews then returns landmarks.arms [null,null] and volume parts.arms 0.0000, the sheet passes, and the only warning is the generic side-view note. A level arm is joined to the torso run on every row it crosses, so frontLandmarks never finds a separate arm run longer than 0.1·Hp. Those arm pixels are then counted as torso width × trunk depth. My cross-check measured head and body with the tool, then added each arm as a solid of revolution (π∫r² along the armStations), counting only the stretch whose axis lies outside the body outline. Tool vs that check: p50 189.1 vs 163.6; p5 179.2 vs 154.0; p95 199.4 vs 173.4; Reeves 164.1 vs 138.3; Coleman 177.1 vs 151.5; largest arm 158.2 vs 135.8. The tool is 15–19% high. Counting the whole arm length (an upper bound) still gives only 143–182. Sweeping f on p50 at 800 px: f 1.74 reads 75.2 (arms found, 67.7°) and f 1.75 reads 83.8 (arms lost, 68.2°), an 11% jump for 0.6% more width. The pessimistic point f 1.786 reads 86.9 with arms lost; the cross-check gives 70.6. The page shows '87–200' and 'about 190 by contact geometry; about 87 if bend falls as with body fat', and the HANDS TO FACE · 87–200 tile. round1.json had already recorded the pose dependence (152.6 at 20°, 191.9 at rest). One caveat on size: part of the gap is a general overcount that also exists when the arms are found (p50 at f=1: 27.3 vs 25.7; arms limit 40.7 vs 37.8). That comes from arm pixels merged with the torso near the shoulder, so a fix will move all three limits a little, not just the face.

Reproduced with s/m2.js. Each met_by figure was drawn at its own height and girths, with the arms at max(35, rest+2) as the limits are, and read by the tool at 1,060 kg/m³ and 7.5% fat, as the limit shapes are. Arms (limit 40.7, band 36.9–41.0): Arnold 35.0 (page 27.5), Oliva 37.0, Bane 37.7, Doomsday 39.2, Hafthor 39.5, Kraemer 40.0, Heath 40.0, Yates 40.6, Lasha 40.9, Cutler 41.1, Wolverine 42.0, Kingpin 42.5, Eddie Hall 42.7, Coleman 44.4. Thighs (limit 46.1, band 42.2–49.2): Coleman 44.4 (page 39.2), Big Ramy 44.6 (39.3), Luke Cage 46.9 (41.1). On the same basis, 8 figures fall under 40.7 rather than the page's 15, and only Arnold is below the arms band. 2 fall under 46.1 rather than 3, and both are inside the thighs band. The rendered page says 'meet this test sooner: 15 of them, from Arnold Schwarzenegger (about 27) up' (forest note) and 'meet the thighs test sooner: three of them, from Ronnie Coleman (about 39) up' (gap copy), neither with any caveat. The limit cards add 'reported girths can run high'. Arnold's own drawer says his drawing holds 34% more than his weight, so the 27-vs-41 contrast mixes a weight-based score with a drawing-based one. The cards credit the gap to shape ('the width sits where…'), but on a consistent basis most of it disappears.
verdicts.better_fix: In compute_limits.js, store chart_figures[id].outline_score: the figure's own drawing scored with the same scoreAt as the limits (after the R2-M1 fix). verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from the model's girth provenance with s/m3b.js (calc kind/owner per site). Of the 24 figures meeting the arms test, only Arnold, Heath, Cutler and Coleman have their own arm, chest and waist girths, and Oliva and Yates have their own partly derived ones. The other 18 are template girths scaled to their weight. Bane is Oliva's template. Doomsday and Wolverine are Yates's. Hafthor, Kraemer, Lasha, Eddie Hall and Kingpin are the largest-arm soldier's. Big Ramy, Luke Cage, the Thing, Thor, Darkseid, the three Hulks, Juggernaut and the Abomination are all Coleman's. For the thighs test, 10 of the 11 are Coleman's template. That is false for 18 of 24 and 10 of 11 figures: template girths are neither the figures' own nor reported. It also presents 11 copies of one shape as 11 independent bodies. This shares sentences with R2-M2, but it is a separate mislabelling.
verdicts.better_fix: In compute_limits.js, record for each met_by id whether the deciding girths are its own (arms: arm_flexed, chest, waist; thighs: thigh) or the template owner (e.calc girth .owner). Write the cards from that: 'As drawn, 24 figures meet it: 6 on their own published girths (Arnold, Oliva, Heath, Yates, Cutler, Coleman); the other 18 are drawn on four template shapes (Coleman's, Yates's, Oliva's, the largest-arm soldier's) scaled to their weights.' For the thighs: '11 figures, all Ronnie Coleman's shape at different sizes; his thigh girth is a fan-site figure (34–36 in).' Replace 'their own girths' with 'those girths'.

return { f: null, reason: 'gap', bestF: fl, bestScore: sl, nextF: fh, nextScore: sh };

Then in app.html drawTarget and export_targets noSheet, handle reason 'gap': 'No outline on this shape measures between ' + sc(sl) + ' and ' + sc(sh) + ': the tool's reading jumps there. verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with s/m1d.js. The fact elbow_flexion_vs_girth_wedge_model defines k = (flexed biceps + flexed forearm) / 0.614 m, with k = 1 at 145° (normal-BMI men) and ansur_overall_median_k 1.086. The median soldier's sum is 0.667 m at 1.755 m, so k = 1.086. settings.json uses 1.786, the k at 100° on the fit's own reference, as a width factor on the median soldier. That gives k = 1.94, and the steep fit then puts φ at 92.0°, not 100°. Read literally, the fit puts the median soldier at 140.1° (between Zwerus's 140° overweight group and 145° normal-BMI group) and reaches 100° at f = 1.7846 / 1.086 = 1.643 (1.602 on absolute girth at 1.80 m). There the tool reads 66.8 (63.6), with the arms found; an arm-aware reading gives 60.8. The fact's own verifier note says the steep crossing is at 'S≈65'. The page's other model also anchors 145° on the soldier, so the 1.786 reading is an arguable choice, but it is not stated, and it contradicts the fact's stated reference. Minor, because it moves only the untested lower end of a band shown without a headline.
verdicts.better_fix: In compute_limits.js, derive the factor instead of hard-coding it: f = Math.pow(Math.tan(40*Math.PI/180)/0.3153, 1/1.69) / kSoldier, where kSoldier = (arm_flexed + forearm at his own height) / 0.614 (gives 1.643). Drop pessimistic_girth_factor from settings.json. Or keep 1.786 and add to the face definition: 'both models put the median soldier at 145°'.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced in the page (s/m4page.js). Largest arm 40, p95 60 and p5 15 each return 'The full-size outline fails the tool's own checks (front and back landmarks line up (within 2% of the height)), so it is not offered.' In Node (s/m2m.js), on the page's own solve-and-refine path: largest arm 40 (f 1.0372) gives 'off: waist (front 395, back 689)', and the front torso widths at those rows are 211 and 211 px, a flat profile. p95 60 gives 'off: waist (front 747, back 395), crotch (front 800, back 598)', with the back view's crotch found 200 px higher. p5 15 gives 'off: neck (front 197, back 219)', with widths 53 and 53 px. renderSheet draws the back as the mirrored front polygons, so the comparison of detected argmin rows flips on one pixel of rasterisation, and on a 1-px difference in the midline crotch scan. A mirror image should never fail this check.
verdicts.better_fix: In measure.js, compare landmarks by width rather than argmin row. For waist and neck, pass if the back view's torso width at the front's landmark row is within max(2 px, 1%) of the back's own minimum, and the same the other way. Scan for the crotch over mid ± 2 px, not a single column. Add the three cases above (largest arm 40, p95 60, p5 15 on the page path) as tests.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced, but narrower than claimed (s/m4m.js, m4m2.js). On assets/rex-turnaround.png with the READINGS skull rows, excluding the tails passes (0.94 at the waist, 0.60 at the hips). Keeping the tails, as the page must, fails with 'depth ÷ front width 0.99 at the waist, 0.94 at the hips; a front or back view in the side position gives about 1', and the front crotch moves from 531 to 400.
